newsitem.title: USA: Morale down in Hong Kong workforce -US firm survey.
newsitem.headline: Morale down in Hong Kong workforce -US firm survey.

text.p: Hong Kong's workforce is showing signs of trepidation before the island's reversion to Chinese sovereignty, according to surveys conducted by a Chicago-based research firm.

International Survey Research Corp. questioned 31,000 Hong Kong employees and 10,000 employees of multinational companies in China about workplace issues. The survey was conducted through the company's Singapore office from 1993 to 1997.
The report said that in 1997, to date, the Hong Kong workforce is reporting substantially lower levels of satisfaction than in 1993 in nearly every facet of their jobs.
In 20 categories, the largest deterioration was registered in "personnel policies, "competitiveness and image," and "performance appraisal.
While Hong Kong's trendline is down, their counterparts in the People's Republic of China (PRC) are reporting higher levels of satisfaction.

In response to the statement: "Looking ahead to the next year or so, I think this company will change for the better", 48 percent of employees surveyed in PRC agreed, compared to 37 percent in Hong Kong.
The largest gap in percpetion occurreed in the area of company image and competitive position.
In "quality of products," 63 percent of respondents in PRC said that their company compares favorabley with its competitors, while only 24 percent of respondents in Hong Kong agreed.
In "Technological Innovation," 55 percent of respondents in PRC cast a vote of coonfidence in their companies, versus 22 percent of respondents in Hong Kong.

"In the Hong Kong of today, anxiety begets anxiety," said John Stanek, chief executive officer of the research firm. "The composite profile for Hong Kong employees mimics that of an enterprise for sale, an organization on the block," he said.
